en: to be sunny; to be sunlit

examples.ko: 우리 집 마당은 하루 종일 양지발라요.
examples.en: Our yard is sunny all day long.

examples.ko: 할머니는 양지바른 마루에 앉아 졸고 계세요.
examples.en: Grandmother is dozing on the sunny porch.

examples.ko: 양지바르고 조용한 동네로 이사 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to move to a sunny, quiet neighborhood.
This room gets a lot of sun, so it's warm even in winter.
If the house is sunny, the potted plants grow well.

examples.ko: 고양이가 양지바른 담 밑에서 자고 있어요.
examples.en: The cat is sleeping under the sunny wall.

explain: '양지바른 곳', '양지바른 마당'처럼 꾸미는 말로 가장 많이 써요. 반대는 해가 안 드는 '음지'예요. '바르다'가 르 불규칙이라 '양지발라요'가 돼요.

phrases.en: I hung the laundry in a sunny spot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '양지바르다'를 꾸미는 말로 쓰는 가장 흔한 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common modifier form of 양지바르다.

phrases.en: The room gets a lot of sun, so it's warm even in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이고, '바르다'가 르 불규칙이라 '양지발라서'가 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: The linking form for giving a reason; because of the 르 irregular, it becomes 양지발라서.

phrases.example: 이 집은 앞이 막혀서 양지바르지 않아요.
phrases.en: This house isn't sunny because the front is blocked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해가 잘 안 드는 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a place that doesn't get much sunlight.

explain_en: It is most often used to modify a noun, as in '양지바른 곳' or '양지바른 마당'. The opposite place is the shady '음지'. Because '바르다' is a 르-irregular verb, it becomes '양지발라요'.

en: to be dim; to be fairly dark

examples.ko: 겨울에는 다섯 시만 되어도 밖이 어둑어둑해요.
examples.en: In winter, it's already dim outside at five o'clock.
As soon as I entered the dim forest, I suddenly got scared.
We played in the park until it got dim.

examples.ko: 저녁 무렵 집 안이 어둑해서 불을 켰어요.
examples.en: It got dim inside the house in the evening, so I turned on the lights.
It's dim outside, so be careful on your way.

examples.ko: 어둑어둑한 골목길을 혼자 걸으려니 조금 무서웠어요.
examples.en: Walking alone down the dim alley was a little scary.

explain: 완전히 깜깜하지는 않고 해 질 무렵이나 새벽처럼 조금 어두운 때에 써요. '어둑어둑하다'처럼 반복해서 말하면 서서히 어두워지는 느낌이 살아나요.

phrases.example: 어둑한 길을 혼자 걸으니 조금 무서웠어요.
phrases.en: Walking alone on the dim road was a bit scary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 완전히 깜깜하지 않은 길이나 장소를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a road or place that is dim but not completely dark.

phrases.en: It's already getting dim outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반복해서 말하면 서서히 어두워지는 느낌이 살아나요.
phrases.nuance_en: Repeating the word brings out the feeling of slowly getting dark.

phrases.en: As the sun set, the sky grew dim.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해 질 무렵에 조금씩 어두워지는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the change of getting a little darker around dusk.

explain_en: It is used for mild darkness, like dusk or early dawn, when it isn't fully dark. Repeating it as '어둑어둑하다' brings out the feeling of slowly getting darker.

examples.en: The dawn sky is faintly getting light.
The building looked dim through the fog.
I vaguely remember things from my childhood.
Moonlight comes faintly into the room.
That person's face comes back to me dimly.

examples.ko: 저녁 무렵 골목에 불빛이 어슴푸레 켜졌어요.
examples.en: Toward evening, lights came on dimly in the alley.

explain: '희미하게'와 비슷하지만 '어슴푸레'는 새벽이나 저녁처럼 어둑한 빛 속에서 흐릿하게 보이는 분위기가 강해요. 기억이 흐릿할 때도 쓸 수 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '어스름'이 있어요.

phrases.en: A light is faintly visible in the distance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어둑한 빛 속에서 흐릿하게 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something looks blurry in dim light.

phrases.en: I vaguely remember things from my childhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기억이 또렷하지 않을 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used when a memory is not clear.

phrases.en: Moonlight shines faintly through the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약한 빛이 희미하게 들어올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when weak light comes in faintly.

explain_en: It is similar to '희미하게' (faintly), but '어슴푸레' carries a stronger feeling of things looking blurry in dim light, like dawn or dusk. You can also use it for a hazy memory. A related word is '어스름'.

examples.en: Lotus flowers have bloomed fully in the pond.
I want to go to the lotus festival in summer.

examples.ko: 연꽃은 진흙 속에서 자라지만 깨끗해 보여요.
examples.en: A lotus grows in mud but looks clean.

examples.ko: 절 마당에 연꽃 등이 걸려 있었어요.
examples.en: Lotus lanterns were hanging in the temple yard.

examples.ko: 그림 속 연꽃이 아주 곱게 그려졌어요.
examples.en: The lotus flower in the painting is drawn very delicately.
My friend sent me a photo of lotus flowers.

explain: '연꽃'은 불교와 관련이 깊어서 절에서 자주 보이는 꽃이에요. 식물은 '연', 잎은 '연잎'이라고 해서 음식 '연잎밥'에도 이 말이 들어가요.

phrases.en: In July the lotus flowers start to bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 필 때 쓰는 가장 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing for a flower blooming.

phrases.en: I received a lotus-shaped plate as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양을 설명할 때 '모양' 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before 모양 to describe a shape.

phrases.en: The pond is full of the scent of lotus flowers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃에서 나는 좋은 냄새를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the pleasant scent coming from the flowers.

explain_en: 연꽃 is closely tied to Buddhism and is often seen at temples. The plant is 연 and its leaf is 연잎, which is also why the dish 연잎밥 has this word in it.

examples.en: Thunder is rumbling among the dark clouds.
The sky rumbled, and soon a shower fell.
The machines at the construction site rumbled all day.

examples.ko: 멀리서 우르릉거리는 소리가 들려서 창문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: I heard a rumbling sound far away, so I closed the window.
It looks like thunder will rumble from the evening.
A truck rumbled through the alley.

explain: 주로 천둥, 큰 차, 기계 소리에 써요. 사람 배에서 나는 소리는 '꾸르륵'이라고 해요. '우르릉대다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: The sky rumbled and then it rained.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우르릉거리다'와 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Interchangeable with '우르릉거리다'.

phrases.en: I hear a rumbling sound from far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 꾸미는 형태로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common form for describing a sound.

phrases.en: The sky is rumbling, so take an umbrella.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 소리가 나는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the sound is going on now.

explain_en: It is mostly used for thunder, big vehicles and machines. A rumbling stomach is '꾸르륵' instead. '우르릉대다' is used with the same meaning.

examples.en: This city has many canals.
Boats move slowly along the canal.

examples.ko: 파나마 운하는 두 바다를 이어 줘요.
examples.en: The Panama Canal connects two oceans.
I walked along the path beside the canal.
People in the past carried goods by canal.
The water in the canal has become clean.

explain: 자연에 있는 물길은 '강'이나 '개천'이라고 하고, 배가 다니거나 물을 보내려고 사람이 판 물길만 운하라고 해요. '파나마 운하', '수에즈 운하'처럼 이름 뒤에 붙여요.

phrases.en: People dug this canal long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 물길을 만든다는 뜻을 보여 주는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This phrase shows that people make a canal by digging.

phrases.en: We crossed the canal over a small bridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운하 위를 지나갈 때 쓰는 일상적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is an everyday phrase for crossing over a canal.

phrases.example: 파나마 운하는 큰 배가 지나가는 길이에요.
phrases.en: The Panama Canal is a route for big ships.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유명한 운하는 이름 뒤에 '운하'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Famous canals take '운하' after their names.

explain_en: A waterway that occurs in nature is called 강 or 개천. Only a channel dug by people for ships or for moving water is called 운하. It follows the name, as in 파나마 운하 and 수에즈 운하.

examples.ko: 호수 위에 백조가 유유히 떠 있어요.
examples.en: A swan is floating leisurely on the lake.

examples.ko: 그는 급한 일이 없다는 듯 유유하게 걸어요.
examples.en: He walks calmly, as if he has nothing urgent to do.

examples.ko: 유유한 강물을 보고 있으면 마음이 편해요.
examples.en: Watching the slowly flowing river makes my mind feel at ease.
That person always looks so unhurried that I envy them.
I spent a calm and relaxed day.
Being unhurried does not mean being lazy.

explain: 거의 '유유히'의 꼴로 많이 써요. 강물, 구름, 걸음처럼 급하지 않고 여유 있는 모습에 쓰고, 급한 상황에서 태연한 모습에도 써요. '유유히 사라지다'가 자주 나오는 표현이에요. 비슷한 말로 '느긋하다', '여유롭다'가 있어요.

phrases.en: The river flows leisurely past the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강물이나 구름처럼 급하지 않게 움직이는 모습에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits things like rivers or clouds that move without hurry.

phrases.en: The thief calmly disappeared.
phrases.nuance_ko: 급한 상황인데도 태연하게 떠나는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone leaves calmly even in a tense situation.

phrases.en: My grandfather walked leisurely in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유유히'와 같은 뜻이지만 '-게' 꼴로 바꿔 써도 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 유유히; the '-게' form is also natural.

explain_en: It is most often used in the form '유유히'. It describes an unhurried, easygoing manner, such as flowing water, clouds or a walk, and also a calm look in an urgent situation. '유유히 사라지다' (to slip away calmly) is a common expression. Similar words are '느긋하다' and '여유롭다'.

examples.en: I went to see a yellow canola flower field on Jeju Island.
In spring, canola blooms all along the roadside.
Oil is pressed from canola seeds and used in cooking.

examples.ko: 유채는 이른 봄부터 노란 꽃이 펴요.
examples.en: Canola produces yellow flowers from early spring.
Many people take photos in the canola field.
This restaurant's canola greens side dish is tasty.

explain: 유채는 봄에 노란 꽃이 피는 식물이라서 제주도 하면 가장 먼저 떠오르는 꽃 중 하나예요. 씨로는 기름을 짜고, 어린 잎은 나물로 먹기도 해요. 같은 노란 봄꽃인 '개나리'는 나무이고 유채는 풀이라 달라요.

phrases.en: The canola flowers sway in the spring breeze.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물 이름보다 노란 꽃 자체를 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common than 유채 when talking about the yellow flower itself.

phrases.en: I took a lot of pictures in the canola flower field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유채꽃이 가득 핀 넓은 밭을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a wide field full of blooming canola flowers.

phrases.en: The canola flowers bloom in April.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 피는 때를 말할 때 '피다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 피다 when talking about when the flowers bloom.

explain_en: 유채 is a plant with yellow spring flowers and is one of the first flowers people think of with Jeju. Its seeds are pressed for oil and its young leaves are eaten as a seasoned vegetable. 개나리, another yellow spring flower, is a shrub, while 유채 is an herbaceous plant.

en: to be dreary; to be dismal; to be gloomy

examples.en: The weather is so dreary that I don't want to go outside.
Even though it's daytime, the sky is dark and gloomy.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 밤에는 골목이 더 음산해 보여요.
examples.en: On rainy nights the alley looks even more eerie.
That movie had a dismal atmosphere.

examples.ko: 음산한 바람이 불더니 갑자기 비가 쏟아졌어요.
examples.en: A gloomy wind blew, and then suddenly the rain poured down.

examples.ko: 그 집은 낮에는 별로 음산하지 않아요.
examples.en: That house doesn't feel very gloomy during the day.

explain: '으스스하다'와 비슷하지만 '음산하다'는 날씨나 분위기가 어둡고 쓸쓸해서 기분이 가라앉을 때 주로 써요. '음산한 날씨', '음산한 분위기'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 모양으로 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '으스스하다'나 '우중충하다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.example: 오늘은 비가 올 것 같은 음산한 날씨예요.
phrases.en: It's a dreary day today, as if it's going to rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 모양으로, 어둡고 쓸쓸한 날씨를 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form used most often to describe dark, bleak weather.

phrases.en: The foggy forest looks gloomy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보이다'를 붙이면 겉모습이 어두워 보인다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 보이다' means something looks dismal from the outside.

phrases.example: 저녁이 되자 음산한 바람이 불기 시작했어요.
phrases.en: In the evening, a gloomy wind began to blow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이 차갑고 으스스하게 느껴질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for a wind that feels cold and eerie.

explain_en: It is similar to '으스스하다' (eerie), but '음산하다' is mainly used when the weather or atmosphere is dark and lonely and brings your mood down. It often appears before a noun, as in '음산한 날씨' or '음산한 분위기'. In everyday talk people also say '으스스하다' or '우중충하다'.

en: to be dense; to be thick

examples.en: It is early morning, so the fog is thick.
I drove slowly along the fog-covered road.
The smoke was so thick that I couldn't see ahead.
I cleaned the storeroom that had been full of dust.

examples.ko: 안개가 자욱하게 낀 날에는 비행기가 늦게 떠요.
examples.en: On days when thick fog sets in, flights leave late.

examples.ko: 호수 위에 물안개가 자욱하더니 곧 사라졌어요.
examples.en: Mist hung thick over the lake and then soon disappeared.

explain: 안개, 연기, 먼지가 어떤 공간에 꽉 차 있을 때 써요. '짙다'는 농도에, '자욱하다'는 가득 퍼진 모습에 초점이 있어요. 부사는 '자욱이'예요.

phrases.example: 자욱한 안개 때문에 앞이 잘 안 보여요.
phrases.en: I can't see ahead well because of the thick fog.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰는 형태로, 안개가 가득 퍼진 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form placed before a noun, describing fog spread thickly everywhere.

phrases.example: 불이 난 뒤 건물 안에 연기가 자욱했어요.
phrases.en: After the fire, the building was filled with thick smoke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거의 장면을 말할 때 쓰는 해요체 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite past form, used to describe a past scene.

phrases.example: 오늘은 안개가 자욱하지 않아서 멀리까지 잘 보여요.
phrases.en: The fog isn't thick today, so I can see far.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가득 차 있지 않다고 부정할 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, saying something is not thick or dense.

explain_en: Use it when fog, smoke or dust fills a space. '짙다' focuses on density, while '자욱하다' focuses on how it spreads and fills the place. The adverb is '자욱이'.

examples.en: The Earth rotates once a day.
Venus rotated very slowly.
The direction in which planets rotate differs from one to another.
The Moon also rotates and goes around the Earth.
Day and night happen because the Earth rotates.
How fast does Saturn rotate?

explain: 자기 둘레를 도는 건 '자전', 다른 별 둘레를 도는 건 '공전'이에요. 지구는 자전하면서 동시에 태양 둘레를 공전해요. 일상 대화에는 거의 안 나오고 과학 수업이나 뉴스에서 써요.

phrases.example: 지구의 자전 때문에 낮과 밤이 생겨요.
phrases.en: Day and night happen because of the Earth's rotation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자전하다'의 명사로, 설명하는 글에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form of '자전하다', common in explanatory writing.

phrases.en: The Earth turns around a tilted axis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자전할 때 중심이 되는 선을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The line that an object spins around when it rotates.

phrases.en: I saw a picture of a rotating planet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자전하다'를 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 모양으로 쓴 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: '자전하다' used as a modifier before a noun.

explain_en: Turning around its own axis is 자전, and going around another body is 공전. The Earth rotates and, at the same time, revolves around the Sun. It hardly shows up in everyday talk; you meet it in science class or the news.

examples.en: I walked along the beach under the blazing sun.

examples.ko: 한여름 햇볕이 작열해서 밖에 나가기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The midsummer sun is scorching, so it's hard to go outside.

examples.ko: 사막의 태양이 작열했지만 우리는 계속 걸었어요.
examples.en: The desert sun blazed, but we kept walking.
The scorching summer passed and the wind turned cool.

examples.ko: 태양이 작열할 때는 모자를 꼭 쓰세요.
examples.en: Please wear a hat when the sun is blazing.

examples.ko: 오후 두 시에는 해가 가장 뜨겁게 작열해요.
examples.en: At two in the afternoon the sun blazes the hottest.

explain: 거의 '작열하는 태양'처럼 해나 불꽃이 뜨겁게 타오를 때 쓰고, 글이나 뉴스 같은 느낌이 강해요. 일상 대화에서는 '해가 쨍쨍하다', '너무 뜨겁다'라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 작열하는 햇살 때문에 모자를 꼭 써야 해요.
phrases.en: Because of the blazing sun, I have to wear a hat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨겁게 타오르는 듯한 햇빛을 글처럼 멋있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A literary way to describe sunlight that burns like fire.

phrases.en: Please don't go outside in the blazing midday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 더운 낮 시간을 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits the hottest part of the day.

phrases.example: 오늘은 해가 쨍쨍해서 빨래가 금방 말라요.
phrases.en: The sun is bright today, so the laundry dries quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이고, 작열하다보다 덜 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday expression, less intense than 작열하다.

explain_en: It is used almost only for a blazing sun or flames, as in '작열하는 태양', and has a written or news-like feel. In daily talk people say '해가 쨍쨍하다' or '너무 뜨겁다'.

examples.ko: 산에 잣나무 숲이 길게 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: A pine forest of Korean nut pines stretches along the mountain.
In autumn, pine nuts grow on the Korean nut pine.
Grandfather planted a Korean nut pine in the yard.
The Korean nut pine stays green even in winter.
The nut pines along the road were covered in snow.
That child grew up straight like a nut pine.

explain: 열매인 '잣'이 열리는 나무예요. 소나무와 비슷해 보이지만 소나무는 잎이 두 개씩, 잣나무는 다섯 개씩 모여 나서 구분할 수 있어요. 발음은 [잔나무]예요.

phrases.en: I walked through a Korean pine forest on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산책이나 여행 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in stories about walks and trips.

phrases.en: My father planted a Korean nut pine in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무를 심는 행동과 함께 쓰는 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A basic phrase for planting trees.

phrases.en: I rested for a moment under the Korean nut pine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무가 있는 장소를 말할 때 조사를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Particles attach to describe where the tree stands.

explain_en: It is the tree that bears pine nuts ('잣'). It looks like a '소나무' (red pine), but needles grow in pairs on a 소나무 and in bundles of five on a 잣나무, so you can tell them apart. It is pronounced [잔나무].

examples.en: When night came, the rain eased off.

examples.ko: 파도 소리가 점점 잦아들더니 바다가 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: The sound of the waves gradually faded, and the sea grew quiet.
Once the fever subsides, you can reduce the medicine.

examples.ko: 아이의 울음이 잦아들 때까지 안아 주었어요.
examples.en: I held the child until the crying died down.
The controversy seemed to be dying down, but then it grew again.
The wind died down, so the ship set off again.

explain: 비, 바람, 소리, 열, 소동처럼 세던 것이 서서히 약해지고 조용해질 때 써요. 한꺼번에 뚝 그치는 게 아니라 점점 줄어든다는 느낌이에요. '가라앉다'와 비슷하게 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The wind died down, so I went outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세던 바람이 점점 약해질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for wind gradually weakening.

phrases.en: My cough just won't subside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약해지지 않고 계속될 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form for something that keeps going without easing.

phrases.en: I'll leave once the rain subsides.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약해진 뒤에 할 일을 말할 때 연결형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Connective form for saying what happens after something eases.

explain_en: Use it when something strong, such as rain, wind, noise, fever or a commotion, gradually weakens and quiets down. It feels like a slow decrease, not a sudden stop. It can be used much like '가라앉다'.
